item.text: {"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"Within the 2023 period, the administration translated several priorities into formal operating machinery, but the supplied record is stronger for design and authorized inputs than for demonstrated execution. The National Public Security Program was issued under López Obrador’s executive authority, made obligatory for federal agencies, assigned monitoring and oversight to ministries, and required implementation through approved budgets (BATCH-0044-E010; BATCH-0044-E011). IMSS-BIENESTAR’s 2023 rules established mandatory operating procedures, budget-linked resource allocation, supervisory visits, performance indicators, corrective measures, complaints channels, audits, and evaluation mechanisms, while preserving congressional budget and administrative constraints (BATCH-0051-E001; BATCH-0051-E004; BATCH-0051-E005). The 2023 budget also allocated resources to 121 social programs, including increases for most priority programs, although these were approved inputs rather than proof of completed implementation (BATCH-0049-E006). A poverty and social-lag framework added reporting obligations for FAIS spending, but the source does not establish compliance or spending quality (BATCH-0012-E001). Security priorities were operationalized through major military-sector spending and National Guard expansion, yet the same evidence records reduced civil-security spending and transfers, incomplete police certification, and limits on effectiveness (BATCH-0016-E007). Formal architecture was also legally contested: the Supreme Court invalidated key portions of the attempted transfer of National Guard budgetary, administrative, organizational, functional, and command control to Sedena, while Plan B electoral reforms were invalidated for legislative-procedure violations (BATCH-0055-E006; BATCH-0055-E008; BATCH-0014-E005). Appointment and institutional functioning were uneven: the administration’s failure to fill IFT and COFECE vacancies impaired their plenaries, although three COFECE commissioners were appointed after a Supreme Court order; the broader vacancy record involved both executive and Senate responsibilities (BATCH-0026-E014; BATCH-0018-E015). An interpretive account further characterizes the governing model as favoring loyal officials and centralization over technical competence, but it is not a complete personnel audit (BATCH-0026-E006). Thus, the evidence supports substantial formal operationalization within executive authority, qualified by congressional, judicial, agency, and subnational constraints, disputed legality, appointment failures, and the absence of independent proof that many prescribed mechanisms functioned as intended.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E010","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0049-E006","BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0016-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0026-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most evidence establishes formal rules, planned or approved resources, and prescribed controls rather than completed compliance, enforcement, service delivery, or outcomes.","Budget evidence concerns approved 2023 allocations and must not be treated as proof of executed spending.","Attribution is strongest for executive programs and policies; IMSS-BIENESTAR rules were issued by the IMSS director, and appointments involved both the Executive and Senate.","The record does not establish the effectiveness or independence of the prescribed audits, evaluations, monitoring, complaint, or corrective mechanisms.","Some mechanisms were legally invalidated or constrained by courts, Congress, autonomous agencies, and subnational actors."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that formal decrees, safeguards, and rules demonstrated executed compliance or functioning enforcement.","Separated approved 2023 budget inputs from implemented action.","Qualified appointment evidence to reflect shared Executive and Senate authority.","Removed unsupported examples and causal overreach while retaining directly supported operationalization and contrary evidence.","Distinguished the inherited National Guard constitutional framework from the administration’s later attempted control transfer."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller ledger would be needed to identify verified 2023 execution records, audit findings, enforcement, service delivery, and corrective actions behind the formal mechanisms.","Further review could clarify the exact scope of executive versus legislative responsibility for each appointment and institutional vacancy.","The supplied record does not independently establish implementation performance across the full portfolio of stated priorities."]}
